question_text: Find the angle between the curves x + y + 2 = 0 and x² + y² − 10y = 0.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say how many points the line and the circle share, how you get both slopes, and what you expect the two angles to be.

steps.label: Find the points of intersection
steps.margin_note: Two marks. The line gives y = −x − 2 directly, so substitution into the circle is one line of algebra. A line cutting a circle meets it at two points, so expect two, and find both.

recall.must_convey: That y = −x − 2 substituted into the circle gives x² + 7x + 12 = 0, so the points are (−3, 1) and (−4, 2).

steps.why: The angle is measured at a shared point, and here there are two of them. Because a chord is symmetric about the perpendicular from the centre to the chord, the angle turns out to be the same at both, but that has to be shown, not assumed.
common_mistakes: Expanding (−x − 2)² as x² + 4 and losing the middle term 4x.
Sign slip in −10(−x − 2), writing −10x − 20 instead of +10x + 20.
Finding only one of the two points.
steps.memory_tip: A straight line is the easiest curve to make the subject, so always substitute the line into the circle, never the circle into the line.

steps.label: Find both slopes there
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The line has one slope everywhere, so only the circle's slope changes from point to point. Note that x + y + 2 = 0 has slope −1.

recall.must_convey: That the line has slope −1 everywhere and the circle has slope x/(5 − y), giving −3/4 at (−3, 1) and −4/3 at (−4, 2).

steps.why: A straight line is its own tangent, so its slope is the same at both points. Only the circle contributes a different slope at each point, which is why both have to be evaluated.
common_mistakes: Reading the slope of x + y + 2 = 0 as 1 instead of −1.
Forgetting the −10y term when differentiating the circle.
Writing the circle slope as x/(y − 5) with the sign reversed.
steps.memory_tip: For ax + by + c = 0 the slope is −a/b, so x + y + 2 = 0 has slope −1.

steps.label: Apply the angle formula
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Both points give tanθ = 1/7, so one angle answers the question. Showing both is the honest way to say the angle does not depend on which end of the chord is used.

recall.must_convey: That tanθ = 1/7 at both points, so θ = Tan⁻¹(1/7).

steps.why: A chord cuts a circle at the same angle at both ends, because the two radii to the ends of a chord make equal angles with it. Getting 1/7 twice is the built-in check on the arithmetic.
common_mistakes: Reporting two different angles because of a sign slip at one of the points.
Writing 1 − m₁m₂ in the denominator instead of 1 + m₁m₂.
Leaving the answer as tanθ = 1/7 without stating the angle.
steps.memory_tip: Two ends of one chord, one angle — if the two values differ, there is an arithmetic slip to find.
lines_compact: The same value comes out at both ends of the chord.

insider_note: Substitute the line into the circle to get the meeting points; there are two, so the working must be done at each. The line's slope is constant, only the circle's changes.
